It is governed by R-A2 and steps A2/A3, not by R-A3's list." |

It changes r2 least: r2's R-A3 first sentence and r2's R-A2 both survive. The other option, all self-performance NONE, would delete R-A3's first sentence. It stays computable as TC-1 1b. | |
17	| **B2** | §3; R-A2 new bullet; R-A5 step 1 ("X of a negative disposition"), rank 1; D4; D5 (ii) | A proposal or attempt is identified **only** when stated in words in the span or section (SOURCE_FACT). An inferred proposal counts as not identified. With an explicit refusal verb (D5 (i)), that gives UNKNOWN. With a bare negation, it gives no disposition (R-A1, NONE). X is the operation named by the **complement** of the refusal expression. | §3: "Identifying a PROPOSAL (D4) … are SOURCE_FACT when the span or section states them in words. Otherwise they are INFERENCE, with the premise quoted." (now only SAME/DISTINCT may be INFERENCE) |
18

20	
21	| Id | r0 extension | r1 (r2 behaviour restored) | Kept because G1–G6 need it | Neutrality follow-up |
22	|---|---|---|---|---|
23	| **M1** | D7 was a closed lexicon for every deontic value, plus the "remains / stays" rule | D7 lists **prohibition operators only**. D9 (obligation) is unchanged. 24	| **M2** | R-X1 limited section use for all acts and norms, with a four-item whitelist | R-X1 now only **forbids** two section uses: a performative or disposition for R-A3 (b), and an operator or status predicate for the G5 boundary. All other section use follows r2. | G1 (no performative from headings), G5 (operator in the span) | none |
25	| **M3** | R-A5 codified all act states. It added an UNKNOWN rule for ACT_REVERSED (A1) and a separate A5 for reported acts. | R-A5 now decides only the G3/G4 competitions: negative disposition vs attempted vs occurred, plus the B1 gate. ACT_REVERSED keeps its r2 meaning with no added condition. ACT_WITHDRAWN without an identified proposal falls to R-A4 (r2). Reported ACT_OCCURRED is r2's meaning. | G3 priority, G4 ATTEMPTED > OCCURRED, B1 gate | none |
26	| **M4** | D11 STATED/MENTIONED applied to all norms, including norms cited as grounds or reported in logs and commits | D11 applies **only to spans carrying a disposition verdict** (the G2 matrix case). Elsewhere every stated norm clause is collected, as in r2. | G2 (R15–R21) | Listed as **TC-5**. New tag `norm.cited_as_ground`. |
27	| **M5** | D8 (ii) made every present/future indicative about an operation a status predicate | D8 (ii) is narrowed to R-A1's own case, a non-commencement statement ("does not begin"). 28	| **M6** | R-S1 counting clause ("one norm observation in every support count") | Removed. `shared_with` keeps both counting options open. | — | none |
29	
30	## 3. Conflicts (`REVIEW-r0.json` `conflicts`)
31	
32	| Id | Conflict | Resolution |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| **C1** | D3 circular: R-A3 (c) required SELF_PERFORMED, and D3 defined it as "R-A3 (a)–(c) hold" | D3 now defines **SELF-PERFORMANCE** by textual form only. (The other review conflict, R-A3 "any other operation → NONE" vs D3's last bullet, is removed by B1.) |
35	| **C2** | D11 (cited grounds MENTIONED) vs R-N1's example "forbids promoting from one" vs D8 (i)'s "the register holds X" | With M4, cited grounds outside verdict spans are STATED, so all three agree. R06/R07's ground clause is a coded norm (STATUS_CONSTRAINT, `cited_as_ground = true`). |
36	| **C3** | D12's negative-verdict phrases ("remains candidate", "stays in …") vs D8 (i) and R-N1's no-re-levelling rule (N2) | A verdict must contain the meta-operation's verb or an eligibility operator **in the span**. Status labels and category letters are status predicates on the item. A new R-N1 example and a D8 (i) entry for category letters were added. The lifted reading is TC-2 2c. |
37	| **C4** | R-A1's "unless an *attempt* is recorded" vs R-A2 / A3's "proposal or attempt" | R-A1 now reads "unless a proposal or attempt is identified (R-A2, §3) and the span is the disposition of it (D5 (ii))". r2 wording struck. |
38	| **C5** | D4 (PREPARED ruling = proposal) vs D6 (a proposal is not ATTEMPTED) | D4 "Proposal vs attempt": a PREPARED ruling is an attempt at its **own** operation and a proposal for **adopt** of itself. Those are never the same (operation, target). D5 notes the same for "NOT ADOPTED". |
39	| **C6** | Merge rule ("coded as X") vs the closed list: an adoption whose content is promotion could be recoded *promote* | Merging replaces only an **unlisted** deciding verb. A listed lemma is never replaced, so "Promotion Review ADOPTED" stays *adopt*. D10 points to the merge rule. |
40	| **C7** | NORM priority incomplete: same-class clauses (R12, R34) and different targets went to step 7 UNKNOWN, contradicting R-A4 | R-N3 step 4: class priority over all clauses, then **first in span order**. The unchosen clauses go to the new `norm.other_clauses`. UNKNOWN only under R-A4. r0 step 7 removed. |
41	| **C8** | ACT operation: no same-step tie-break; "highest step" undefined | R-A5 step 4: rank 1 is highest. Gated candidates rank below rank 3. Same rank: first in span order. The others are recorded as `SPLIT_REQUIRED`. |
42	
43	## 4. Selected nonblocking items
44	
45	| Id | Item | Change |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| **N3** | Tag bare authorize performatives | New `norm.performative_token`. "Bare" is defined in §2. TC-4 now has 4b (exclude bare) and 4c (exclude all performative-token norms). |
48	| **N6** | REPORTED vs SELF_PERFORMED for rows reproducing another actor's ruling | D3 "Reproduced operative text": a row's own ruling, reproduced or attributed, is a self-performance. A named other ruling or instrument as the source makes it REPORTED. Naming the actor is never a REPORTED sign. New `act.attributed_to`. TC-1 1d. The REPORTED signs are also made explicit (headline participles and present passives are not signs). |
49	| **D13** | Two-operation rule | D13 (i) coordinated verbs under one predicate form one clause (`plan + implement`). (ii) Separate operators form separate clauses. (iii) An operation named by a noun or option label is the target ("ANNOTATE is adopted" → adopt / ANNOTATE). |
50	| **NEG** | Negation, only as needed for R01 | D7: *may* within the scope of a preceding negative quantifier (*no <noun> may …*) is a prohibition operator. Nothing else on negation was changed. |
51	
52	## 5. THEORY-CHOICES
53	
54	- TC-1 rewritten for the negative case, plus 1d (B1, N6).
55	- TC-2: 2c added (C3).
56	- TC-3 unchanged.
57	- TC-4: performative_token, 4b/4c (N3).
58	- **TC-5 new** (M4 / N5).
59	- **TC-6 new** (M5 / N4).
60	
61	Tag-and-compute is kept throughout.
62	
63	## 6. Gap records re-run under r1
64	
65	| Gap | Record | r1 answer | Change vs r0 |
66	|---|---|---|---|
67	| G1 | R15–R18 | act NONE, `SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`, operation *classify* (the category letter comes first in the span; step 4), `SPLIT_REQUIRED: recommend`, `state_if_extended = ACT_OCCURRED` | operation tie now decided |
68	| G1 | R19–R21 | act NONE, `SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`, *classify*, `state_if_extended = ACT_OCCURRED` | tie decided |
69	| G1 | R27 | act NONE, `SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`, *apply* §12. `state_if_extended = ACT_ATTEMPTED` / PREPARED (the R-83 section marks the ruling PREPARED), `later_disposition`: adopted, R-86. "rather than superseding" is a contrastive. Norm NONE; "it APPLIES §12" in `norm.indicative`. | `state_if_extended` new; norm no longer a D8 (ii) status predicate (M5) |
70	| G2 | R15–R18 | ELIGIBLE, VERDICT, *promote*, target = the row's behaviour. Category letter and (R18) "already ARB-adopted" in `other_clauses`. | none |
71	| G2 | R19 | **STATUS_CONSTRAINT**, STATUS_PREDICATE, `status: category C`, target Registration ≠ Delivery. "Stays in ADR-MP-06", "→ Candidate Pattern" in `other_clauses`. | was INELIGIBLE (C3) |
72	| G2 | R20, R21 | **STATUS_CONSTRAINT**, STATUS_PREDICATE, `status: category D`. "Remains Candidate" in `other_clauses`. R21: "replaced only on repeated evidence" in `norm.indicative`. | was INELIGIBLE (C3) |

75	| G3 | R29 | act NONE, `basis = NONE`. Norm NONE ("would" is a modal). | none |

139	  - (ii) the deontic operator or status predicate that decides REQUIRED vs PROHIBITED vs STATUS_CONSTRAINT (R-N2).
140	
141	  Every other use of the section follows r2 (e.g. R-A2's "in the span or its section").
142	
143	## 5. Definitions `[r3]`
144	
145	- **D1. REGISTER ROW** `[r3-G1]`. A span whose `section` heading is exactly a register ruling identifier (`## R-<number>`, with nothing else in the heading). These are not register rows: a section about a ruling's attachment ("## R-36 promotion matrix (adopted by R-36): …"), session logs, commits, plans, or any null section.
146	
147	- **D2. PERFORMATIVE** `[r3-G1]`. A verb, participle or nominalization in the span by which the span's own instrument does the act it names. Examples: present-tense ruling text ("X adopts …", "… is adopted"), a headline participle ("SLICE X AUTHORIZED"), or "is authorized to …" in the instrument's operative text.
148	
149	- **D3. SELF-PERFORMANCE; act.basis** `[r3-G1]` `[r1-fix-C1]` `[r1-fix-N6]`.
150	  - **SELF-PERFORMANCE.** The span's own text constitutes the act. It contains a PERFORMATIVE (D2), or a negative disposition expression (D5; a withdrawal or reversal expression) in the present tense, in headline form, or in the instrument's operative text, **and** no REPORTED sign holds. This definition does not refer to R-A3.
151	  - **REPORTED signs.** Any one of these makes the act REPORTED:
152	    - (i) a finite past or perfect verb for the act ("was adopted", "ruled", "has been issued"), or a participle used as a narrative clause ("Then R-90 itself withdrawn"). A headline participle or present passive ("SLICE X AUTHORIZED", "X is adopted") is **not** a sign;
153	    - (ii) another instrument, record or document, or an earlier date, named as where the act was constituted ("(adoption act: R-86)", "per R-44", "in the commission's own artefacts");
154	    - (iii) conduct verbs ("ran", "appended", "probed").
155	  - **Reproduced operative text** `[r1-fix-N6]`. A span that reproduces operative text and names its issuer ("RULING AS ISSUED, VERBATIM", "IN THE BOARD'S OWN WORDS", "(Principal Architect instruction)") is:
156	    - a SELF-PERFORMANCE if the reproduced text is the ruling of the register row it stands in, i.e. no other ruling or instrument is named as its source;
157	    - REPORTED if another ruling or instrument is named as its source.
158	
159	    Naming the issuing actor is never by itself a REPORTED sign. The issuer is recorded in `act.attributed_to`.
160	  - **Values:**
161	    - **REPORTED:** a REPORTED sign holds.
162	    - **SELF_PERFORMED:** a SELF-PERFORMANCE for which R-A3 (a) and (b) hold.
163	    - **SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3:** a SELF-PERFORMANCE for which R-A3 (a) or (b) fails, positive or negative. Examples: a register row that classifies, recommends, applies, approves, retires, or declines to resolve; a matrix cell that recommends or classifies; a row that "expressly does NOT promote".
164	    - **NONE:** no act.
165	
166	- **D4. PROPOSAL** `[r3-G3]` `[r1-fix-B2]` `[r1-fix-C5]`. Text in the span or section stating **in words** that performing X on the target was **put forward for decision**. This includes:
167	  - a motion, request, offered option or option set;
168	  - an issued PREPARED ruling (a proposal for its adoption);
169	  - a recommendation;
170	  - a question put to the decider of whether to do X.
171	
172	  A mere possibility, a statement that X has not happened, or a proposal the coder can only infer from context, is not a proposal.
173	  - **Proposal vs attempt** `[r1-fix-C5]`. One instrument can be both, **for different operations**. An issued PREPARED ruling is:
174	    - (i) an ACT_ATTEMPTED of the operation it performs (e.g. *authorize*, target WP-4C-1; D6);
175	    - (ii) a proposal for *adopt*, target = the ruling itself, which the adopting authority may adopt, hold or refuse.
176	
177	    (i) and (ii) never share an (operation, target). D6's "a proposal is not ATTEMPTED" means that putting X forward for decision is not an attempt at X.
178	
179	- **D5. REFUSAL EXPRESSION / DISPOSITION** `[r3-G3]`.
180	  - (i) **Explicit refusal verb:** *decline(s), reject(s/ed), refuse(s/d)*, "will not", "is/are NOT ADOPTED", "expressly NOT [X]".
181	  - (ii) **Negated X as a disposition:** a negation of X ("X is not superseded") counts only when the span is the decision on the proposal. Either the span states a deciding act ("ruled", "held", "decided") whose content is the negation, or the span is the operative or headline text of the register row that the section identifies as deciding that proposal. `[r1-fix-B2]` The proposal must be identified as SOURCE_FACT (§3).
182	  - **Never dispositions:** continuative or non-perfective negations ("has not been", "not yet", "remains / still not", "un-"), contrastives ("rather than X"), and reasons against an unchosen option.
183	  - `[r1-fix-C5]` "NOT ADOPTED" on a PREPARED instrument is both a D6 non-effect marker for the instrument's own operation and, where the adoption proposal is identified, a refusal of *adopt* (target = the instrument). These are different (operation, target) pairs (D4).
184	
185	- **D6. ACT_ATTEMPTED; PREPARED; FAILED** `[r3-G4]`.
186	  - **ACT_ATTEMPTED:** the span or section records that an actor **initiated** X (issued, filed, submitted, tried, ran) **and** a source statement says the initiation **did not by itself take effect**. There are two kinds:
187	    - **PREPARED:** the instrument is marked "PREPARED", "NOT ADOPTED", "awaiting adoption", or as needing a further act to take effect.
188	    - **FAILED:** the attempt is recorded as rejected or errored by a mechanism or an actor (e.g. "refused: …", "record unchanged").
189	  - **Not ATTEMPTED:**
190	    - a proposal (offering X for decision is not an attempt at X; D4);
191	    - an intended or planned act;
192	    - a conditional or provisoed act (R-A6).
193	
194	- **D7. PROHIBITION OPERATOR** `[r3-G5]` `[r1-fix-M1]` `[r1-fix-NEG]`. Matching is case-insensitive.
195	  - *must not, shall not, may not, no … shall, is/are forbidden / prohibited, forbids …-ing, NOT PERMITTED*; imperative *never …* / *do not …*.
196	  - `[r1-fix-NEG]` The permission modal *may*, when a preceding negative quantifier or adverb takes it in its scope (*no <noun> may …*, *nothing may …*, *never may …*), is a prohibition operator. Example: "no self-issued act may adopt" is PROHIBITED, `about_operation = adopt`, `about_actor` = a self-issued act.
197	  - `[r1-fix-M1]` D7 is not a lexicon for PERMITTED, AUTHORIZED, UNAUTHORIZED or DELEGATED. Those keep their r2 meaning. ELIGIBLE / INELIGIBLE: see D12. REQUIRED: see D9.
198	
199	- **D8. STATUS PREDICATE; STATUS_CONSTRAINT** `[r3-G5]` `[r3-G6]`. A STATUS PREDICATE is a predicate, with no deontic operator, that assigns an item or operation a **standing in the governance order**. There are three kinds:
200	  - (i) **Status label.** A lifecycle, standing or class label: open, closed, frozen, deferred, retired, held, in force, governing, binding, permanent, standard, candidate; `[r1-fix-C3]` a category letter in a classification; "remains / stays <label>"; scope statements such as "the register holds X".
201	  - (ii) `[r1-fix-M5]` **Non-commencement statement.** The case R-A1 names: a present-tense indicative, with no modal, stating that an operation does not begin (*does not begin / start / commence / proceed*; "no RED begins"). Other present- or future-tense indicatives about whether an operation takes place ("it APPLIES §12", "no observable behaviour changes until 7C", "Implementation continues under …") are **not** status predicates. They are listed in `norm.indicative` (TC-6).
202	  - (iii) **Listed performative.** A performative or participle of a listed R-A3 operation other than *authorize* (adopted, superseded, annotated, registered), `[r1-fix-B1]` or a negative disposition of one (not superseded, NOT ADOPTED, declines to adopt), predicated of a named object. Its `basis = PERFORMATIVE_ONLY`.
203	
204	  Statements that a condition, guard or proviso is or is not met are **facts, not status predicates**. STATUS_CONSTRAINT is the value for (i)–(iii).
205	
206	- **D9. REQUIRED** `[r3-G5]`. An obligation operator attached to an operation: *must, shall, is/are required to, is obliged to, has to, MUST BE …-ed, requires <actor> to …, mandatory*.
207	
208	- **D10. SAME EVENT / DISTINCT** `[r3-G3]` `[r3-G6]`.
209	  - **SAME EVENT:** two candidate acts in one span are the same event if one is the deciding or performing act whose **stated content** is the performance, refusal, withdrawal or reversal of the other ("rules that X is not superseded"; "held it — not adopted"). Coordinated verbs with one actor and one object ("confirms and adopts") are also one event. `[r1-fix-C6]` The coded operation follows the merge rule (R-A5 step 1).
210	  - **DISTINCT:** otherwise. This covers different actors, different times, or an act given as the **ground** of another ("withdrawn … because the Authority ruled …").
211	
212	- **D11. STATED vs MENTIONED** `[r3-G2]` `[r1-fix-M4]` `[r1-fix-C2]`.
213	  - **Scope.** D11 applies **only to a span that carries a disposition verdict** (D12), such as a promotion-matrix row.
214	  - **MENTIONED** (in such a span): content the span names, quotes or proposes **as the object** of the verdict or recommendation (a candidate behaviour's name, a proposed one-line rule text, a quoted principle), and content cited as evidence for the verdict (an evidence column).
215	  - **STATED:** all other content of the span.
216	  - In every other span the r2 reading holds: each normative clause the span states is collected, including clauses cited as grounds and clauses reported from another actor. `norm.cited_as_ground` tags the former (TC-5). So R-N1's example "forbids promoting from one" (a ground clause in a session log), and D8 (i)'s "the register holds X" (a ground clause in R06/R07), are coded norms.
217	
218	- **D12. DISPOSITION VERDICT; ELIGIBLE / INELIGIBLE** `[r3-G2]` `[r1-fix-C3]`.
219	  - **Disposition verdict:** a classification or recommendation that assigns an item an outcome of a meta-operation under decision in the section, without performing that operation, **and** that contains, in the span, the meta-operation's verb (positive, imperative or negated: "PROMOTE", "promote to …", "NOT promoted", "do not promote") or an eligibility operator (*eligible, not eligible, qualifies, does not qualify*).
220	  - A phrase that only predicates a status label of the item ("Remains Candidate", "Stays in ADR-MP-06", a category letter) is a STATUS PREDICATE (D8 (i)) on the item, not a verdict. Its `about_operation` is `status: <label>` (R-N1).
221	  - **ELIGIBLE:** a positive verdict or a positive eligibility operator: the item qualifies for, or is recommended for, operation X.
222	  - **INELIGIBLE:** a negated verdict or a negative eligibility operator.
223	  - `about_operation` = X. A verdict is never evidence that X occurred (R-A1).
224	
225	- **D13. LITERAL ATTACHMENT** `[r3-G2]`. The operation that a norm clause governs is:
226	  - the verb the operator modifies;
227	  - for a verdict, the meta-operation the verdict concerns;
228	  - for a status predicate, the operation named in it, or else `status: <label>`.
229	  - `[r1-fix-D13]` **Two operations named.**
230	    - (i) One operator, verdict or predicate governing coordinated verbs is **one** clause. `about_operation` lists the verbs in span order, joined by " + " ("AUTHORIZED TO PLAN AND IMPLEMENT" → `plan + implement`).
231	    - (ii) Separate operators governing separate verbs are **separate** clauses ("MAY BE PLANNED AND MUST NOT BE STARTED" → PERMITTED *plan* and PROHIBITED *start*; R-N3 step 4).
232	    - (iii) An operation named only by a noun or a name (a subject, an object or an option label) supplies `about_target`, never `about_operation`. `about_operation` is the operation of the predicate word: "ANNOTATE is adopted" → `about_operation = adopt`, `about_target = ANNOTATE` (the option).
233	
234	- **D14. SHARED SPAN** `[r3-G6]`. Two or more records whose `span` fields are verbatim-identical within the same source and section.
235

# SCHEMA-r3 (repair r1)

Change key:
- Unmarked text is SCHEMA-r2 verbatim.
- `[r3-Gn]` marks text added or modified by the first r3 draft (r0) to close gap Gn in `GAPS.md`.
- `[r1-fix-<id>]` marks text changed by this repair (r1) of r0. The ids are listed in `CHANGELOG-r1.md`: B = blocking item, M = minimality revert, C = conflict, N = neutrality item, D13 = two-operation rule, NEG = negation. r0 text that r1 removes is not shown here. CHANGELOG-r1 records it.
- Where an r2 sentence is modified, the r2 wording is struck through as `~~…~~` and the new wording follows.

---

## 1. Unit: the individuated span record
- One record = one **verbatim source span**, the smallest sufficient span (1aw).
- **Fields:** `record_id` · `v1_event_ids` (lineage) · `source` (file + blob id) · `section` · `span` (verbatim; markdown emphasis markers may be stripped, and that must be disclosed).
- **Uniqueness:** (span, operation, target) must be unique. Events resolving to one span are **one record**. A span carrying an act clause and a norm clause stays **one record with both components**.
  - `[r3-G6]` "Events resolving to one span are one record" applies to **SAME-EVENT** candidates (§5 D10). A span that records two or more **DISTINCT** acts (D10) that differ in operation or target yields one record per (operation, target). Those records **share** the span and are coded under **R-S1**.

## 2. Two independent components per record

**ACT: does the span record an act that actually happened?**
- `act.state` ∈ {ACT_OCCURRED, ACT_ATTEMPTED, ACT_REFUSED, ACT_WITHDRAWN, ACT_REVERSED, NONE, UNKNOWN}.
- `act.operation`: what act (open vocabulary; the v1 operation list is preferred).
- `act.actor` · `act.target` · `act.quote`.
- `[r3-G1]` `[r1-fix-C1]` `act.basis` ∈ {REPORTED, SELF_PERFORMED, SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3, NONE} (D3). Required on every record. When `act.basis = SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`, `act.state` is NONE, but `act.operation` and `act.state_if_extended` are still filled in (R-A3, R-A5 step 2).
- `[r1-fix-B1]` `act.state_if_extended`: required if and only if `act.basis = SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`. It is the state R-A5 step 3 would assign if the R-A3 scope gate (R-A5 step 2) were not applied: ACT_OCCURRED, ACT_ATTEMPTED, ACT_REFUSED, ACT_WITHDRAWN, ACT_REVERSED or UNKNOWN. It is **not** `act.state`. It exists so that THEORY-CHOICES TC-1 alternative 1c can be computed.
- `[r1-fix-N6]` `act.attributed_to` (optional): the actor that the span or its row names as the issuer of reproduced operative text ("RULING AS ISSUED, VERBATIM", "IN THE BOARD'S OWN WORDS", "(Principal Architect instruction)"). It does not change `act.basis` (D3). It exists for TC-1 alternative 1d.
- `[r3-G4]` `act.attempt_kind` ∈ {PREPARED, FAILED} (D6). Required if and only if `act.state = ACT_ATTEMPTED` `[r1-fix-B1]` or `act.state_if_extended = ACT_ATTEMPTED`.
- `[r3-G4]` `act.later_disposition` (optional): if the span **or its section** records a later act that gave the attempted act effect or denied it effect (adopted / held / withdrawn by …), give that act's identifier and a quote. This does **not** change `act.state` (R-A6).

**NORM: what normative / deontic content does the span state?**
- `norm.deontic` ∈ {PERMITTED, REQUIRED, PROHIBITED, AUTHORIZED, UNAUTHORIZED, ELIGIBLE, INELIGIBLE, DELEGATED, STATUS_CONSTRAINT, NONE, UNKNOWN}.
  - `[r3-G5]` REQUIRED, PROHIBITED and STATUS_CONSTRAINT are defined in D7–D9. `[r3-G2]` ELIGIBLE / INELIGIBLE are defined in D12. `[r1-fix-M1]` The other values keep their r2 meaning. r3 gives no lexicon for them.
- `norm.about_operation` · `norm.about_actor` · `norm.about_target` (the *governed* act).
  - `[r3-G2]` `about_operation` is fixed by **literal attachment** (D13, R-N1). For STATUS_CONSTRAINT with no governed operation named, write `status: <verbatim status label>`.
- `norm.stated_by`: the act or actor stating it, if identifiable.
  - `[r3-G4]` If the span or its section marks the stating instrument PREPARED (D6), `stated_by` carries the marker verbatim, e.g. `ARB CHIEF (PREPARED)`.
- `norm.quote`.
- `[r3-G6]` `norm.basis` ∈ {OPERATOR, VERDICT, STATUS_PREDICATE, PERFORMATIVE_ONLY} (D7, D8, D12, R-N3). Required whenever `norm.deontic` is not NONE / UNKNOWN.
- `[r1-fix-N3]` `norm.performative_token` ∈ {true, false}. Required whenever `norm.basis` is filled. It is true when the chosen clause's normative word is the **same token** by which the record's R-A3 act is performed. This covers every PERFORMATIVE_ONLY clause, and an *authorize* performative coded OPERATOR (R-N3 step 5). Otherwise it is false. A **bare authorize performative** is a clause with `performative_token = true`, `deontic = AUTHORIZED`, and no governed operation stated in the span (`about_operation` with status NOT_EVIDENCED), e.g. "Slice 7C AUTHORIZED".
- `[r1-fix-M4]` `norm.cited_as_ground` ∈ {true, false}. Required whenever `norm.basis` is filled. It is true when the chosen clause stands in a segment that the span marks as the ground of, or evidence for, another statement ("because …", "since …", "on the ground that …", "GROUNDS:", "Evidence:", an evidence column). Otherwise it is false (TC-5).
- `[r1-fix-C7]` `norm.other_clauses`: a list of the norm clauses that R-N3 step 1 collected but did not choose. Each entry has `deontic`, `about_operation`, `about_target`, `basis`, `performative_token` and `quote`. It is empty otherwise. The primary NORM fields above stay single-valued.
- `[r1-fix-M5]` `norm.indicative`: a list of {`quote`, `operation`} for each present- or future-tense indicative in the span that has no modal, states whether an operation takes place, and is **not** a status predicate under D8 (ii). These are not coded as norms (TC-6). It is empty otherwise.
- `[r3-G6]` `norm.shared_with`: list of the other `record_id`s that share this span (R-S1); empty otherwise.

**Both components may be non-NONE for the same record.** They are coded **independently**.
- `[r3-G4]` The NORM component records **stated content**, whether or not the act that stated it took effect. It does not code the norm's force. The act's effectiveness is recorded only in the ACT component (`ACT_ATTEMPTED` / `attempt_kind`). See THEORY-CHOICES TC-3.

## 3. Epistemic status per coded field
Each coded field carries a status ∈ {SOURCE_FACT, INFERENCE, UNKNOWN, NOT_EVIDENCED}. An INFERENCE states its premise. No silent defaults.
- `[r3-G3]` `[r1-fix-B2]` A PROPOSAL or attempt (D4, R-A2) is identified **only as SOURCE_FACT**: the span or its section states it in words. A proposal or attempt that could only be inferred counts as **not identified** (R-A2, R-A5 step 3). Judging SAME EVENT vs DISTINCT (D10) is SOURCE_FACT when the span or section states it in words. Otherwise it is INFERENCE, with the premise quoted.

## 4. Critical rules
- **R-A1.** **Never infer an ACT from a NORM.** "X is authorized to begin" is a NORM (AUTHORIZED); it is not evidence that X began. ~~"Implementation does not begin" is a NORM (PROHIBITED / a status constraint); it is **not** an ACT_REFUSED unless an attempt is recorded.~~ `[r3-G5]` `[r1-fix-C4]` "Implementation does not begin" is a NORM: **STATUS_CONSTRAINT** (D8 (ii)), because it has no deontic operator (R-N2). It would be PROHIBITED only if it read "must not / shall not begin". It is **not** an ACT_REFUSED unless a **proposal or attempt** is identified (R-A2, §3) and the span is the disposition of it (D5 (ii)).
- **R-A2.** ACT_REFUSED / ACT_WITHDRAWN require an **identified proposal or attempt** in the span or its section.
  - `[r3-G3]` "Proposal" is defined in D4. ACT_REFUSED also requires a **refusal expression that disposes of that proposal** (D5). A negation that only reports non-occurrence so far ("has not been issued", "remains unauthorized", "not yet") is **never** a refusal. A reason given against an option that was not chosen, with no refusal expression ("X would blur chronology"), is **not** a refusal. Its act is coded NONE.
  - `[r1-fix-B2]` "Identified" means **stated in words** in the span or section (SOURCE_FACT, §3). An inferred proposal is not identified. The refused operation X is the operation named by the **complement of the refusal expression** (R-A5 step 1). It is never taken from the section or from what the refused item would have done.
- **R-A3.** A register row **that itself performs** a norm-making act (adopts, authorizes, registers, supersedes, annotates) is an ACT_OCCURRED of that operation. Its stated content is additionally a NORM.
  - `[r3-G1]` `[r1-fix-B1]` **Scope (closed, and the same for positive and negative acts).** R-A3 applies only when **all** of the following hold:
    - (a) the section is a REGISTER ROW (D1);
    - (b) the **span itself** contains either
      - (b+) a PERFORMATIVE (D2) of one of the five listed operations, matched by lemma: *adopt, authorize, register, supersede, annotate*; or
      - (b−) a **negative disposition expression** (a refusal expression, D5, or a withdrawal or reversal expression) whose operation X (R-A5 step 1) is one of the same five lemmas: "ADR-T14 is not superseded", "NOT ADOPTED", "declines to adopt …".

      Inflections and nominalizations count. Synonyms do not ("approve", "confirm" alone, "classify", "recommend", "apply", "file", "retire", "hold", "direct", "defer", "promote", "resolve" are **not** listed). The negative verb itself (*decline, reject, refuse, withdraw, reverse*) is never the listed operation;
    - (c) the act is a SELF-PERFORMANCE (D3), not REPORTED.

    It is **not** applied by analogy. A performative or disposition found only in the section, row heading or annotation label, and not in the span, does not satisfy (b).

    **Symmetry.** A span that self-performs any other operation, **positively or negatively**, or that self-performs outside a register row, is coded `act.state = NONE` with `act.basis = SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`. The operation and `act.state_if_extended` are recorded (R-A5 step 2). Example: in the R-36 row, "Promoted into AST-013 …" and "Expressly NOT promoted: …" are **both** NONE / SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3, because *promote* is not listed. Adding operations to the list is a schema revision, not a coder judgement (THEORY-CHOICES TC-1).
  - `[r3-G6]` `[r1-fix-B1]` **"Its stated content is additionally a NORM"** is mandatory whenever R-A3 applies, under (b+) or (b−). Code the NORM by R-N3. Because a listed performative, or a negative disposition of a listed operation, always yields at least a norm clause (D8 (iii)), an R-A3 record never has `norm.deontic = NONE`. If the only basis is the performative itself, `norm.basis = PERFORMATIVE_ONLY`.
- **R-A4.** UNKNOWN when the span does not decide. It is counted, and excluded from support counts.

- **R-A5. `[r3-G3]` `[r3-G4]` ACT priority order.**
  - `[r1-fix-M3]` **What this rule decides.** R-A5 decides only the competitions that G3 and G4 raise: a negative disposition vs an occurrence vs an attempt on the same (operation, target), plus the R-A3 scope gate. It adds **no condition** to any state. ACT_OCCURRED for reported acts and ACT_REVERSED keep their r2 meaning (§2). ACT_REFUSED and ACT_WITHDRAWN keep R-A2.
  - **Step 1. Candidates.**
    - Collect the candidate acts the span supports. Acts cited only as **evidence or grounds** for the span's principal content (e.g. in an evidence column or a "because …" clause) are not candidates for this record. They may be their own records.
    - Merge SAME-EVENT candidates (D10). DISTINCT candidates belong to separate records (§1, R-S1).
    - `[r1-fix-C6]` **Merge rule.** When the deciding verb is **not** a listed R-A3 lemma (e.g. *rule, decide, hold, determine, confirm*), and its stated content is the performance, refusal, withdrawal or reversal of operation X, the act is coded **as X** ("rules that X is not superseded" → *supersede*; "confirms and adopts" → *adopt*). A listed lemma is **never** replaced by merging. If the deciding verb is itself a listed lemma, the operation is that lemma and the decided content is its target ("Promotion Review ADOPTED" → *adopt*, target = the Promotion Review). Merging can therefore never move an act off the R-A3 list.
    - `[r1-fix-B2]` **X of a negative disposition.** X is the operation named by the **complement** of the refusal, withdrawal or reversal expression: "declines to resolve an ambiguity …" → *resolve*; "is not superseded" → *supersede*; "NOT ADOPTED" → *adopt*. If the complement is a noun that names no operation ("R-90 … withdrawn"), X is the expression's own lemma (*withdraw*, *reverse*, *refuse*) and the noun is the target.
  - **Step 2. `[r1-fix-B1]` Scope gate.** A candidate that is a SELF-PERFORMANCE (D3), positive or negative, and fails R-A3 (a) or (b), is removed from step 3. The record is coded `act.state = NONE`, `act.basis = SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`, `act.operation = X`. `act.state_if_extended` is the result step 3 would give it. REPORTED candidates are never gated, whatever their operation, polarity or section.
  - **Step 3. Ranks.** Apply the ranks to each remaining candidate. **The first rank that matches decides.**

| Rank | Condition (span, plus section only where stated) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Negative disposition** of X: a refusal expression (D5), a withdrawal expression or a reversal expression | **Refusal:** ACT_REFUSED if a PROPOSAL for X is identified (R-A2, §3). An explicit refusal verb (D5 (i)) without one: UNKNOWN. A negated X without one is not a disposition (D5 (ii), R-A1) and is not a rank-1 candidate. **Withdrawal:** ACT_WITHDRAWN if the withdrawn proposal or attempt is identified (R-A2); otherwise R-A4 applies. **Reversal:** ACT_REVERSED, as in r2 |
| 2 | Initiation of X, plus a non-effect marker (D6) | ACT_ATTEMPTED, with `attempt_kind` |
| 3 | X occurred: REPORTED (D3), or R-A3 (a)–(c) hold | ACT_OCCURRED |
| 4 | No candidate remains | NONE. `basis = NONE`, or `SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3` if step 2 removed a candidate |

  - **Step 4. `[r1-fix-C8]` Choosing among candidates on a single record.** If candidates for different (operation, target) remain and the record is the only record on the span:
    - code the candidate of the **highest rank**. Rank 1 is the highest and rank 3 the lowest. A candidate removed by the scope gate ranks below rank 3, and is ranked among other gated candidates by its `state_if_extended`;
    - between candidates of the same rank, code the one whose expression occurs **first in the span**;
    - add `SPLIT_REQUIRED: <operation>` for each other candidate to the premise of `act.operation`.
  - **Consequences of the order.**
    - A refusal (rank 1) outranks a register row's own performance (rank 3). A register row that negatively disposes of a **listed** X is coded ACT_REFUSED (or ACT_WITHDRAWN / ACT_REVERSED) on X. A row that negatively disposes of an **unlisted** X is NONE / SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3, exactly like a row that performs an unlisted X (R-A3 Symmetry).
    - An ATTEMPTED act (rank 2) outranks ACT_OCCURRED (rank 3). A PREPARED instrument is never coded ACT_OCCURRED of its own operation.

- **R-A6. `[r3-G4]` PREPARED and other non-effective acts.**
  - An act is ACT_ATTEMPTED only on a **non-effect marker in the source** (D6). The coder never judges, on their own account, whether an actor had the capability or authority to act. Without a marker, an act by any actor is coded at `[r1-fix-M3]` rank 3.
  - A conditional or provisoed authorization ("authorized … provided …") is **not** ATTEMPTED. The act is coded at rank 3. The condition belongs to the NORM.
  - A later adoption, hold or withdrawal recorded in the section is a **separate act**. It is recorded in `act.later_disposition` and does not convert the attempted act to ACT_OCCURRED.

- **R-N1. `[r3-G2]` Level of the governed act.**
  - `norm.about_operation` is the operation that the span's deontic operator, verdict or status predicate **attaches to grammatically** (D13). It is never raised to a meta-act or lowered to a substantive behaviour.
  - Rule content that the span only MENTIONS (D11) supplies `about_target`. It never supplies a separate norm, and its internal modals are not coded.
  - **Examples:**
    - "PROMOTE" applied to a named candidate behaviour attaches to *promote*, with target = that behaviour.
    - "may begin RED" attaches to *begin RED*.
    - "forbids promoting from one" attaches to *promote*.
    - `[r1-fix-C3]` "Remains Candidate" in a promotion matrix row is a status label on the row's behaviour (`status: Candidate`). It is not lifted to *promote* (D12).

- **R-N2. `[r3-G5]` REQUIRED vs PROHIBITED vs STATUS_CONSTRAINT.**
  - The deontic value is read from the **span**. `[r1-fix-M2]` The section may not supply the operator or the status predicate (R-X1).
  - If an obligation operator (D9) or a prohibition operator (D7) attaches to an operation, the value is REQUIRED or PROHIBITED.
  - If there is no deontic operator, and a STATUS PREDICATE (D8) is predicated of an item or operation, the value is STATUS_CONSTRAINT.
  - A status noun or adjective ("standard", "permanent", "candidate", "in force", "binding", "frozen") is a status predicate even if it implies conformity. It is never REQUIRED unless an obligation operator attaches to an operation.

- **R-N3. `[r3-G2]` `[r3-G5]` `[r3-G6]` NORM decision procedure and priority order.**
  1. Collect the norm clauses in the span: deontic operators (`[r1-fix-M1]` D7 for PROHIBITED, D9 for REQUIRED, and the other r2 deontic values in their r2 sense), disposition verdicts (D12), status predicates (D8), and listed performatives (D8 (iii)). `[r1-fix-M4]` In a span that carries a disposition verdict, skip MENTIONED content (D11).
  2. If there are none, the value is NONE.
  3. For each clause, set `about_operation` by literal attachment (R-N1, D13), and `about_target` = the item the clause is predicated of. In a table or matrix row, that is the row's subject item.
  4. `[r1-fix-C7]` **Choose one clause.** Over all clauses of the span, whatever their targets, take the highest class: **OPERATOR > VERDICT > STATUS_PREDICATE > PERFORMATIVE_ONLY.** Between clauses of the same class, take the clause that occurs **first in the span**.
  5. Map the chosen clause:
     - operator → the value it expresses (D7, D9, or the r2 value);
     - verdict → ELIGIBLE / INELIGIBLE;
     - status predicate or performative-only → STATUS_CONSTRAINT.

     Exception: a performative of *authorize* is a deontic operator (AUTHORIZED, `basis = OPERATOR`), because "authorized" is in the deontic vocabulary. `[r1-fix-N3]` It gets `performative_token = true`.
  6. Record `norm.basis`, `norm.performative_token` and `norm.cited_as_ground`.
  7. `[r1-fix-C7]` Record every other clause from step 1 in `norm.other_clauses`.

  `[r1-fix-C7]` The value is UNKNOWN only under R-A4: when the span does not decide whether a clause is present or what it states. Several clauses never make the value UNKNOWN.

- **R-S1. `[r3-G6]` Shared-span rule.** When two or more records share one verbatim span:
  - **ACT:** each record codes **only** the act for its own (operation, target). An act is never coded on more than one record.
  - **NORM:** the norm clause(s) of the span, selected by R-N3, are coded **identically on every record sharing the span**. Each record lists the others in `norm.shared_with`. The coder does not choose which record "owns" the norm.

- **R-X1. `[r3-G1]` `[r3-G5]` `[r1-fix-M2]` What the section may not supply.** The section (heading and surrounding source text of the same section) may **not** supply:
  - (i) the performative or negative disposition expression for R-A3 (b);
  - (ii) the deontic operator or status predicate that decides REQUIRED vs PROHIBITED vs STATUS_CONSTRAINT (R-N2).

  Every other use of the section follows r2 (e.g. R-A2's "in the span or its section").

## 5. Definitions `[r3]`

- **D1. REGISTER ROW** `[r3-G1]`. A span whose `section` heading is exactly a register ruling identifier (`## R-<number>`, with nothing else in the heading). These are not register rows: a section about a ruling's attachment ("## R-36 promotion matrix (adopted by R-36): …"), session logs, commits, plans, or any null section.

- **D2. PERFORMATIVE** `[r3-G1]`. A verb, participle or nominalization in the span by which the span's own instrument does the act it names. Examples: present-tense ruling text ("X adopts …", "… is adopted"), a headline participle ("SLICE X AUTHORIZED"), or "is authorized to …" in the instrument's operative text.

- **D3. SELF-PERFORMANCE; act.basis** `[r3-G1]` `[r1-fix-C1]` `[r1-fix-N6]`.
  - **SELF-PERFORMANCE.** The span's own text constitutes the act. It contains a PERFORMATIVE (D2), or a negative disposition expression (D5; a withdrawal or reversal expression) in the present tense, in headline form, or in the instrument's operative text, **and** no REPORTED sign holds. This definition does not refer to R-A3.
  - **REPORTED signs.** Any one of these makes the act REPORTED:
    - (i) a finite past or perfect verb for the act ("was adopted", "ruled", "has been issued"), or a participle used as a narrative clause ("Then R-90 itself withdrawn"). A headline participle or present passive ("SLICE X AUTHORIZED", "X is adopted") is **not** a sign;
    - (ii) another instrument, record or document, or an earlier date, named as where the act was constituted ("(adoption act: R-86)", "per R-44", "in the commission's own artefacts");
    - (iii) conduct verbs ("ran", "appended", "probed").
  - **Reproduced operative text** `[r1-fix-N6]`. A span that reproduces operative text and names its issuer ("RULING AS ISSUED, VERBATIM", "IN THE BOARD'S OWN WORDS", "(Principal Architect instruction)") is:
    - a SELF-PERFORMANCE if the reproduced text is the ruling of the register row it stands in, i.e. no other ruling or instrument is named as its source;
    - REPORTED if another ruling or instrument is named as its source.

    Naming the issuing actor is never by itself a REPORTED sign. The issuer is recorded in `act.attributed_to`.
  - **Values:**
    - **REPORTED:** a REPORTED sign holds.
    - **SELF_PERFORMED:** a SELF-PERFORMANCE for which R-A3 (a) and (b) hold.
    - **SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3:** a SELF-PERFORMANCE for which R-A3 (a) or (b) fails, positive or negative. Examples: a register row that classifies, recommends, applies, approves, retires, or declines to resolve; a matrix cell that recommends or classifies; a row that "expressly does NOT promote".
    - **NONE:** no act.

- **D4. PROPOSAL** `[r3-G3]` `[r1-fix-B2]` `[r1-fix-C5]`. Text in the span or section stating **in words** that performing X on the target was **put forward for decision**. This includes:
  - a motion, request, offered option or option set;
  - an issued PREPARED ruling (a proposal for its adoption);
  - a recommendation;
  - a question put to the decider of whether to do X.

  A mere possibility, a statement that X has not happened, or a proposal the coder can only infer from context, is not a proposal.
  - **Proposal vs attempt** `[r1-fix-C5]`. One instrument can be both, **for different operations**. An issued PREPARED ruling is:
    - (i) an ACT_ATTEMPTED of the operation it performs (e.g. *authorize*, target WP-4C-1; D6);
    - (ii) a proposal for *adopt*, target = the ruling itself, which the adopting authority may adopt, hold or refuse.

    (i) and (ii) never share an (operation, target). D6's "a proposal is not ATTEMPTED" means that putting X forward for decision is not an attempt at X.

- **D5. REFUSAL EXPRESSION / DISPOSITION** `[r3-G3]`.
  - (i) **Explicit refusal verb:** *decline(s), reject(s/ed), refuse(s/d)*, "will not", "is/are NOT ADOPTED", "expressly NOT [X]".
  - (ii) **Negated X as a disposition:** a negation of X ("X is not superseded") counts only when the span is the decision on the proposal. Either the span states a deciding act ("ruled", "held", "decided") whose content is the negation, or the span is the operative or headline text of the register row that the section identifies as deciding that proposal. `[r1-fix-B2]` The proposal must be identified as SOURCE_FACT (§3).
  - **Never dispositions:** continuative or non-perfective negations ("has not been", "not yet", "remains / still not", "un-"), contrastives ("rather than X"), and reasons against an unchosen option.
  - `[r1-fix-C5]` "NOT ADOPTED" on a PREPARED instrument is both a D6 non-effect marker for the instrument's own operation and, where the adoption proposal is identified, a refusal of *adopt* (target = the instrument). These are different (operation, target) pairs (D4).

- **D6. ACT_ATTEMPTED; PREPARED; FAILED** `[r3-G4]`.
  - **ACT_ATTEMPTED:** the span or section records that an actor **initiated** X (issued, filed, submitted, tried, ran) **and** a source statement says the initiation **did not by itself take effect**. There are two kinds:
    - **PREPARED:** the instrument is marked "PREPARED", "NOT ADOPTED", "awaiting adoption", or as needing a further act to take effect.
    - **FAILED:** the attempt is recorded as rejected or errored by a mechanism or an actor (e.g. "refused: …", "record unchanged").
  - **Not ATTEMPTED:**
    - a proposal (offering X for decision is not an attempt at X; D4);
    - an intended or planned act;
    - a conditional or provisoed act (R-A6).

- **D7. PROHIBITION OPERATOR** `[r3-G5]` `[r1-fix-M1]` `[r1-fix-NEG]`. Matching is case-insensitive.
  - *must not, shall not, may not, no … shall, is/are forbidden / prohibited, forbids …-ing, NOT PERMITTED*; imperative *never …* / *do not …*.
  - `[r1-fix-NEG]` The permission modal *may*, when a preceding negative quantifier or adverb takes it in its scope (*no <noun> may …*, *nothing may …*, *never may …*), is a prohibition operator. Example: "no self-issued act may adopt" is PROHIBITED, `about_operation = adopt`, `about_actor` = a self-issued act.
  - `[r1-fix-M1]` D7 is not a lexicon for PERMITTED, AUTHORIZED, UNAUTHORIZED or DELEGATED. Those keep their r2 meaning. ELIGIBLE / INELIGIBLE: see D12. REQUIRED: see D9.

- **D8. STATUS PREDICATE; STATUS_CONSTRAINT** `[r3-G5]` `[r3-G6]`. A STATUS PREDICATE is a predicate, with no deontic operator, that assigns an item or operation a **standing in the governance order**. There are three kinds:
  - (i) **Status label.** A lifecycle, standing or class label: open, closed, frozen, deferred, retired, held, in force, governing, binding, permanent, standard, candidate; `[r1-fix-C3]` a category letter in a classification; "remains / stays <label>"; scope statements such as "the register holds X".
  - (ii) `[r1-fix-M5]` **Non-commencement statement.** The case R-A1 names: a present-tense indicative, with no modal, stating that an operation does not begin (*does not begin / start / commence / proceed*; "no RED begins"). Other present- or future-tense indicatives about whether an operation takes place ("it APPLIES §12", "no observable behaviour changes until 7C", "Implementation continues under …") are **not** status predicates. They are listed in `norm.indicative` (TC-6).
  - (iii) **Listed performative.** A performative or participle of a listed R-A3 operation other than *authorize* (adopted, superseded, annotated, registered), `[r1-fix-B1]` or a negative disposition of one (not superseded, NOT ADOPTED, declines to adopt), predicated of a named object. Its `basis = PERFORMATIVE_ONLY`.

  Statements that a condition, guard or proviso is or is not met are **facts, not status predicates**. STATUS_CONSTRAINT is the value for (i)–(iii).

- **D9. REQUIRED** `[r3-G5]`. An obligation operator attached to an operation: *must, shall, is/are required to, is obliged to, has to, MUST BE …-ed, requires <actor> to …, mandatory*.

- **D10. SAME EVENT / DISTINCT** `[r3-G3]` `[r3-G6]`.
  - **SAME EVENT:** two candidate acts in one span are the same event if one is the deciding or performing act whose **stated content** is the performance, refusal, withdrawal or reversal of the other ("rules that X is not superseded"; "held it — not adopted"). Coordinated verbs with one actor and one object ("confirms and adopts") are also one event. `[r1-fix-C6]` The coded operation follows the merge rule (R-A5 step 1).
  - **DISTINCT:** otherwise. This covers different actors, different times, or an act given as the **ground** of another ("withdrawn … because the Authority ruled …").

- **D11. STATED vs MENTIONED** `[r3-G2]` `[r1-fix-M4]` `[r1-fix-C2]`.
  - **Scope.** D11 applies **only to a span that carries a disposition verdict** (D12), such as a promotion-matrix row.
  - **MENTIONED** (in such a span): content the span names, quotes or proposes **as the object** of the verdict or recommendation (a candidate behaviour's name, a proposed one-line rule text, a quoted principle), and content cited as evidence for the verdict (an evidence column).
  - **STATED:** all other content of the span.
  - In every other span the r2 reading holds: each normative clause the span states is collected, including clauses cited as grounds and clauses reported from another actor. `norm.cited_as_ground` tags the former (TC-5). So R-N1's example "forbids promoting from one" (a ground clause in a session log), and D8 (i)'s "the register holds X" (a ground clause in R06/R07), are coded norms.

- **D12. DISPOSITION VERDICT; ELIGIBLE / INELIGIBLE** `[r3-G2]` `[r1-fix-C3]`.
  - **Disposition verdict:** a classification or recommendation that assigns an item an outcome of a meta-operation under decision in the section, without performing that operation, **and** that contains, in the span, the meta-operation's verb (positive, imperative or negated: "PROMOTE", "promote to …", "NOT promoted", "do not promote") or an eligibility operator (*eligible, not eligible, qualifies, does not qualify*).
  - A phrase that only predicates a status label of the item ("Remains Candidate", "Stays in ADR-MP-06", a category letter) is a STATUS PREDICATE (D8 (i)) on the item, not a verdict. Its `about_operation` is `status: <label>` (R-N1).
  - **ELIGIBLE:** a positive verdict or a positive eligibility operator: the item qualifies for, or is recommended for, operation X.
  - **INELIGIBLE:** a negated verdict or a negative eligibility operator.
  - `about_operation` = X. A verdict is never evidence that X occurred (R-A1).

- **D13. LITERAL ATTACHMENT** `[r3-G2]`. The operation that a norm clause governs is:
  - the verb the operator modifies;
  - for a verdict, the meta-operation the verdict concerns;
  - for a status predicate, the operation named in it, or else `status: <label>`.
  - `[r1-fix-D13]` **Two operations named.**
    - (i) One operator, verdict or predicate governing coordinated verbs is **one** clause. `about_operation` lists the verbs in span order, joined by " + " ("AUTHORIZED TO PLAN AND IMPLEMENT" → `plan + implement`).
    - (ii) Separate operators governing separate verbs are **separate** clauses ("MAY BE PLANNED AND MUST NOT BE STARTED" → PERMITTED *plan* and PROHIBITED *start*; R-N3 step 4).
    - (iii) An operation named only by a noun or a name (a subject, an object or an option label) supplies `about_target`, never `about_operation`. `about_operation` is the operation of the predicate word: "ANNOTATE is adopted" → `about_operation = adopt`, `about_target = ANNOTATE` (the option).

- **D14. SHARED SPAN** `[r3-G6]`. Two or more records whose `span` fields are verbatim-identical within the same source and section.

That choice was flagged as building H-D's view into the observations. r3 restricts R-A3 to its literal text (closed list, register rows only, performative in the span) and does not extend it. It tags every act with `act.basis`.

14	- inside the scope (register row, listed operation, in the span), both are acts: ACT_OCCURRED / ACT_ATTEMPTED for positives, ACT_REFUSED / ACT_WITHDRAWN / ACT_REVERSED for negatives;

In R-36, "Promoted into …" and "Expressly NOT promoted: …" are **both** non-acts. |

It weakens tests of H-D's "norms change only through acts", because many norm changes then have no observed act. |

32	Example: a promotion matrix adopted by a register ruling recommends that a named behaviour be promoted. Is the record then carrying a norm on that **behaviour** (e.g. REQUIRED: reuse before create), or only a verdict on the **meta-act** (ELIGIBLE: promote)?

# THEORY-CHOICES (r3, repair r1)

SCHEMA-r3 gives every coding question an answer, or UNKNOWN. Six questions remain that are **theoretical, not coding, questions**. Answering any of them would decide part of what H-D and H-B disagree about. r3 does not answer them. Instead, it records the distinguishing information as tags, so that each alternative below can be computed from the coded data at analysis time. The analysis must state which alternative it uses, and should report results under each alternative.

r1 keeps this tag-and-compute approach. It corrects TC-1 (the negative case was missing and the r0 description was inaccurate), extends TC-2 and TC-4, and adds TC-5 and TC-6. TC-5 and TC-6 are the choices that r0 had built into D11 and D8 (ii) without listing them.

---

## TC-1 (G1): Does an instrument's self-performance count as an act? `[r1-fix-B1]` `[r1-fix-N6]`

This choice is **inherited from r2, not made by r3**. r2's R-A3 already makes one choice: a register row that self-performs one of five listed norm-making operations is ACT_OCCURRED. That choice was flagged as building H-D's view into the observations. r3 restricts R-A3 to its literal text (closed list, register rows only, performative in the span) and does not extend it. It tags every act with `act.basis`.

**r1 correction: negative dispositions.** r0 coded a span's own refusal, withdrawal or reversal of **any** operation, in **any** section, as an act, while it limited positive self-performance to the five listed operations in register rows. That was alternative 1c applied to negative acts only, and it was not disclosed. r1 scopes negative and positive self-performance **identically** (SCHEMA R-A3 (b+)/(b−), R-A5 step 2):
- inside the scope (register row, listed operation, in the span), both are acts: ACT_OCCURRED / ACT_ATTEMPTED for positives, ACT_REFUSED / ACT_WITHDRAWN / ACT_REVERSED for negatives;
- outside the scope, both are `act.state = NONE`, `basis = SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`, with the would-be state in `act.state_if_extended`.

The TASK offered two symmetric options. r1 chose this one because it changes r2 least: r2's R-A3 first sentence (listed positive self-performance in register rows is ACT_OCCURRED) and r2's R-A2 (refusals are acts when a proposal is identified) both survive. The other option, coding all self-performance as NONE, would delete R-A3's first sentence. That option remains computable as alternative 1b.

| Alternative | What counts as an act | Consequence for what the data can show |
|---|---|---|
| **1a. r2 as written (r3 default coding)** | `basis = REPORTED` (any operation, positive or negative, any section) + `basis = SELF_PERFORMED` (a register row's own performance **or own refusal / withdrawal / reversal** of a listed operation) | Norm-making acts are observed wherever a register row performs, or negatively disposes of, a listed operation. Every such act is a register act by construction, so "norms change through acts" is partly true by definition for register rows. That part cannot count as evidence for H-D over H-B. Positive and negative dispositions are treated alike: R-77's "ADR-T14 is not superseded" is an act (ACT_REFUSED supersede), like a row that supersedes. In R-36, "Promoted into …" and "Expressly NOT promoted: …" are **both** non-acts. |
| **1b. Reported acts only** | `basis = REPORTED` | The data show only acts that some text reports as having happened. The register's own rulings, positive and negative, stop being act observations, so norm-making acts become rare. This **under-counts** what both hypotheses agree exists. It weakens tests of H-D's "norms change only through acts", because many norm changes then have no observed act. |
| **1c. Extended self-performance** | 1a + `basis = SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3`, taking the state from `act.state_if_extended` | Classifications, recommendations, applications, approvals, retirements and matrix verdicts all become acts, **and so do their negative counterparts** ("Expressly NOT promoted" → ACT_REFUSED promote, if a proposal is stated; else UNKNOWN). R01 ("declines to resolve …") becomes UNKNOWN, because no proposal to resolve is stated (R-A2). Act counts rise most for governance-text operations. This extends the flagged H-D-favouring convention further, in both directions alike. |
| **1d. Reproduced rulings as reported** (modifier on 1a / 1c) | As 1a or 1c, but records with `act.attributed_to` filled are treated as REPORTED | Rows that reproduce an issuer's words ("RULING AS ISSUED, VERBATIM", "IN THE BOARD'S OWN WORDS", "(Principal Architect instruction)") count as reports of an act by that issuer, not as the row's own act. Under 1b + 1d these rows (R02, R23, R26) **survive** as act observations. Under 1b alone they do not. The default (D3) treats them as self-performances, because the reproduced text is the row's own ruling. |

All four are computable from `act.basis`, `act.state_if_extended`, `act.attributed_to` and `act.operation`. r3's coded `act.state` follows 1a only because that is the unrevised r2 text, now applied symmetrically.

---

## TC-2 (G2): Are behaviours named in an adopted instrument substantive norms the record carries? `[r1-fix-C3]`

Example: a promotion matrix adopted by a register ruling recommends that a named behaviour be promoted. Is the record then carrying a norm on that **behaviour** (e.g. REQUIRED: reuse before create), or only a verdict on the **meta-act** (ELIGIBLE: promote)?

r3 codes by literal attachment (R-N1). The verdict is coded on *promote*. The behaviour is MENTIONED (D11) and goes in `about_target`. A status label on the behaviour ("Remains Candidate", "Stays in ADR-MP-06", a category letter) is coded as a status label on the behaviour (`status: <label>`), not as a verdict on *promote* (D12, r1). r3 does **not** decide whether adoption of the instrument incorporates the mentioned behaviour as an in-force substantive norm.

| Alternative | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **2a. No incorporation.** Only stated norms count. | The data show the record carrying norms **about governance meta-acts** wherever a behaviour is handled by promotion or adoption. They show substantive norms only where a span states them. This looks closer to H-D's "the governed work is outside what the record needs to contain". The cause is partly that the substantive text lives in other documents, which this rule does not follow. |
| **2b. Incorporation by reference.** An adopted instrument's positive verdicts count as substantive norms on the mentioned behaviour. | The data show the record carrying norms on governed work, which looks closer to H-B. This requires an inferred deontic value that no span states (REQUIRED? PERMITTED?), so those observations would be INFERENCE throughout. |
| **2c. Status labels in a review read as verdicts** (r1; modifier on 2a / 2b) | Status labels that a review matrix assigns to a candidate ("Remains Candidate", category C / D) are read as INELIGIBLE *promote*. This is the reading r0 built into D12. It moves those records from the behaviour level to the meta-act level, toward H-D's framing. r1's default keeps the literal level. |

All are computable. 2b = records with `norm.deontic = ELIGIBLE` and `basis = VERDICT`, joined to the adopting act's record. 2c = records in a section carrying disposition verdicts, with `basis = STATUS_PREDICATE` (primary clause or in `norm.other_clauses`), recoded as INELIGIBLE.

---

## TC-3 (G4): Does a norm stated by a non-effective (PREPARED) act have force?

r3 codes the act as ACT_ATTEMPTED / PREPARED. It codes the stated content (e.g. AUTHORIZED) as a NORM, with `stated_by` carrying the PREPARED marker. It does not code **force**.

| Alternative | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **3a. Force follows the making act's status.** PREPARED norms are not in force until a later act gives them effect. | The data can test whether work conforms to *effective* norms only. A prepared authorization followed by work would count as non-conformity. |
| **3b. Force follows stated content.** | Prepared and adopted norms are treated alike. Any difference between them, the thing H-D predicts matters, cannot appear in the analysis. |
| **3c. Force undecided; report separately.** | The cost is smaller cells. The difference between prepared and adopted norms is shown, not assumed. |

Choosing 3a in the schema would build H-D's second bullet ("force depends on the status of the act that made it") into the observations. Choosing 3b would rule it out by definition.

---

## TC-4 (G6): Do performative-only norms count as norm observations? `[r1-fix-N3]`

r2's R-A3 second sentence requires a NORM on every self-performing row. When a row's only normative words are the performative itself ("ANNOTATE is adopted", "adopts R-81 through R-85", "ADR-T14 is not superseded"), r3 codes STATUS_CONSTRAINT with `norm.basis = PERFORMATIVE_ONLY`.

**r1 addition.** An *authorize* performative is coded AUTHORIZED with `basis = OPERATOR` (R-N3 step 5). A **bare** authorize performative also has no governed operation stated in the span.

| Alternative | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **4a. Count them.** | Every such act generates a co-located norm. Act–norm co-occurrence is then partly definitional, and cannot be used as evidence for H-D's "norms change only through acts". |
| **4b. Exclude bare performatives.** Exclude `basis = PERFORMATIVE_ONLY` and bare authorize performatives. | Norm counts contain only norms with some textual content beyond the performative. "AUTHORIZED TO PLAN AND IMPLEMENT" stays, because it names the governed operations. |
| **4c. Exclude every performative-token norm.** Exclude every record with `performative_token = true`. | The strictest form: no norm that is stated by the same word that performs the act is counted, even with a named governed operation. Authorizations, the most common operation in this register, then appear as norms only where a separate clause states them. |

Under 4b and 4c, a record whose primary clause is excluded takes, as its norm, the first entry of `norm.other_clauses` that is not excluded, if there is one. All three are computable from `norm.basis`, `norm.performative_token`, `about_operation` status and `norm.other_clauses`.

---

## TC-5 (new in r1): Do norms cited as grounds, or reported from another actor, count? `[r1-fix-M4]`

r0's D11 treated content "cited as evidence" as MENTIONED in **every** span, and STATED as content the instrument "asserts as its own". That could drop every norm a session log or commit reports, and every norm given as a ground, leaving norms mainly in governance instruments (review item N5). r1 restricts D11 to spans carrying a disposition verdict (the G2 case). Everywhere else, every norm clause the span states is coded, as under r2, and ground clauses are tagged `norm.cited_as_ground = true`.

| Alternative | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **5a. Count all stated norms (r3 default coding)** | Norms in session logs, commits and ground clauses are observed ("ES-006.1 forbids promoting from one"; "the register holds constitutional decisions"). Norms then appear also in the narration of work, which gives H-B's "the record carries or references both" more material. |
| **5b. Exclude ground clauses** (`cited_as_ground = true`) | Norms invoked only as reasons drop out. The record's norms are then those it asserts directly. |

All three are computable from `norm.cited_as_ground` and `section`.

---

## TC-6 (new in r1): Do prospective indicatives about work count as norms? `[r1-fix-M5]`

The other indicatives are not coded as norms. They are listed, with their operation, in `norm.indicative`.

- Making the norm component a list. This is a structural change beyond the six gaps. `other_clauses` is an auxiliary field: the primary component stays single-valued, and only the unchosen clauses are recorded.
- A substantive tie rule (e.g. "the most restrictive clause wins"). That is a theory of norm precedence. Span order is neutral, and the other clauses are kept.

---

## r1 repairs not covered above

- **D3 circularity (C1).** Self-performance is now defined by textual form alone. `SELF_PERFORMED` vs `SELF_PERFORMED_OUTSIDE_RA3` is then the R-A3 scope test applied to it. R-A3 (c) refers to self-performance, not to a basis value, so the definition no longer refers to itself. *Rejected:* keeping "SELF_PERFORMED = R-A3 (a)–(c) hold", which is circular.
- **Reproduced rulings (N6).** A register row that reproduces its own ruling verbatim, or names its issuer, is the instrument of that ruling, so its text is a self-performance. Naming the issuer is recorded in `act.attributed_to`, and the reported reading is computable (TC-1d). Only a named other ruling or instrument as the source makes the act REPORTED. *Why:* register rows always carry an issuer, so "an actor is named" cannot distinguish reports from rulings. "Another instrument is named" can. *Rejected:* treating every attribution as REPORTED. That would make most rulings reports and is a theory choice; it is kept as 1d.
- **R-A1 vs R-A2 (C4).** R-A1 now says "proposal or attempt", matching R-A2, which is the specific rule for refusals.
- **Section use (M2).** Only the two restrictions G1 and G5 need are kept: no performative or disposition from the section for R-A3, and no operator or status predicate from the section for the G5 boundary. Every other section use reverts to r2.
- **Not repaired here** (outside the TASK's list): D1's dependence on dataset heading format; TC-2 2b's missing join key; and an overlap that r1 noticed between D6 FAILED ("refused: …" by a mechanism) and rank-1 refusal. See CHANGELOG-r1.md.

## 1. Unit: the individuated span record
- One record = one **verbatim source span**, the smallest sufficient span (1aw).
- **Fields:** `record_id` · `v1_event_ids` (lineage) · `source` (file + blob id) · `section` · `span` (verbatim; markdown emphasis markers may be stripped, and that must be disclosed).
- **Uniqueness:** (span, operation, target) must be unique. Events resolving to one span are **one record**. A span carrying an act clause and a norm clause stays **one record with both components**.

## 2. Two independent components per record

**ACT: does the span record an act that actually happened?**
- `act.state` ∈ {ACT_OCCURRED, ACT_ATTEMPTED, ACT_REFUSED, ACT_WITHDRAWN, ACT_REVERSED, NONE, UNKNOWN}.
- `act.operation`: what act (open vocabulary; the v1 operation list is preferred).
- `act.actor` · `act.target` · `act.quote`.

**NORM: what normative / deontic content does the span state?**
- `norm.deontic` ∈ {PERMITTED, REQUIRED, PROHIBITED, AUTHORIZED, UNAUTHORIZED, ELIGIBLE, INELIGIBLE, DELEGATED, STATUS_CONSTRAINT, NONE, UNKNOWN}.
- `norm.about_operation` · `norm.about_actor` · `norm.about_target` (the *governed* act).
- `norm.stated_by`: the act or actor stating it, if identifiable.
- `norm.quote`.

**Both components may be non-NONE for the same record.** They are coded **independently**.

## 3. Epistemic status per coded field
Each coded field carries a status ∈ {SOURCE_FACT, INFERENCE, UNKNOWN, NOT_EVIDENCED}. An INFERENCE states its premise. No silent defaults.

## 4. Critical rules
- **R-A1.** **Never infer an ACT from a NORM.** "X is authorized to begin" is a NORM (AUTHORIZED); it is not evidence that X began. "Implementation does not begin" is a NORM (PROHIBITED / a status constraint); it is **not** an ACT_REFUSED unless an attempt is recorded.
- **R-A2.** ACT_REFUSED / ACT_WITHDRAWN require an **identified proposal or attempt** in the span or its section.
- **R-A3.** A register row **that itself performs** a norm-making act (adopts, authorizes, registers, supersedes, annotates) is an ACT_OCCURRED of that operation. Its stated content is additionally a NORM.
- **R-A4.** UNKNOWN when the span does not decide. It is counted, and excluded from support counts.

8	
9	- **B1. The R-A3 scope is not closed for negative dispositions.** The rules let a span's own text count as an act when it refuses, withdraws or reverses *any* operation, in *any* section. Positive self-performance is limited to five operations in register rows. This extends the flagged text-as-act convention by analogy, which R-A3 itself forbids. It contradicts R-A3's own "any other operation → NONE" sentence, it is mislabelled `SELF_PERFORMED`, and THEORY-CHOICES TC-1 does not disclose it.
10	- **B2. G3 is not closed for R01.** The span can still be coded either UNKNOWN or ACT_REFUSED, because §3 lets a PROPOSAL be identified by INFERENCE, and because it is not clear which operation X is.

42	## 2. Minimality
43	
44	Every change carries an `[r3-Gn]` tag. Several of them reach beyond the cells that disagreed and change coding elsewhere:
45	
46	1. **D7 is now a complete closed lexicon** for every deontic value (PERMITTED, AUTHORIZED, ELIGIBLE, DELEGATED, the "remains" rule). G5 needed only the REQUIRED / PROHIBITED / STATUS_CONSTRAINT boundary. Side effect: R01's "no self-issued act may adopt" matches only PERMITTED "may", because "no … may" is not listed.
47	2. **R-X1 limits section use for every norm and act**, not only R-A3 performatives and the G5 operator question.
48	3. **R-A5 codifies every act state.** This includes a new UNKNOWN rule for ACT_REVERSED (A1) and A5 for reported acts. G3 needed only REFUSED vs OCCURRED, and G4 needed only A4.
49	4. **D11 STATED/MENTIONED applies to all norms**, including any norm a span cites as evidence or grounds. It reaches session logs and commits, well beyond the G2 matrix rows.
50	5. **D8(ii) generalises R-A1's single example** to every present- or future-tense indicative about an operation.
51	6. **R-S1's counting clause** prescribes analysis, not coding. It is minor and tied to G6.
52	
53	Items 1–5 can be defended as needed to make the procedures operational. They should be disclosed as scope extensions, because they change values outside the 36-record disagreement set.
54	
55	## 3. Neutrality
56	
57	**R-A3 scope.**
58	- The positive side is properly closed: a closed lemma list, register rows only, the performative must be in the span, no heading imports, and `basis` tags that make TC-1 computable.
59	- **The negative side is open (blocking, B1).**
60	  - D3's last bullet makes a self-performed refusal `SELF_PERFORMED`, governed by A2/A3 "not by R-A3's list". A1 has no basis or section restriction for withdrawals and reversals. Because A1–A3 come before A7, text that refuses or withdraws *any* operation, in *any* section, becomes an act.
61	  - R-A3's own sentence says "A span that self-performs any other operation … is coded `act.state = NONE`". The two directly conflict.
62	  - In this corpus: R-36's "**Expressly NOT promoted:** …" is D5(i) "expressly NOT [X]", with the matrix as the D4 proposal. That gives ACT_REFUSED *promote*. The same row's "Promoted into AST-013 … 6 behaviours" is A7 NONE. Refusals to promote are acts, promotions are not.
63	  - This is TC-1 alternative 1c (the extension TC-1 itself calls H-D-favouring), applied to negative dispositions only. It is undisclosed, and `SELF_PERFORMED` is defined in D3 as "R-A3 (a)–(c) hold", so the label is wrong.
64	  - It is computable only by combining `state` with `operation`, which TC-1 does not mention.
65	
66	**"Governed act" level.**
67	- Literal attachment is a sound neutral principle, and it works for R15–R18 ("PROMOTE" is literally the verb).
68	- **N2:** for R19–R21 the literal text is a status label on the behaviour ("Remains Candidate", "Stays in ADR-MP-06"). Under D8(i) and R-N1 that is STATUS_CONSTRAINT (`status: candidate`) on the behaviour. D12 lists exactly these phrases as INELIGIBLE verdicts, and VERDICT > STATUS_PREDICATE then lifts them to the meta-act *promote*. 69	- TC-2 is correctly left open. Its 2b computation needs a join key (the parsed "(adopted by R-36)" heading) and an unspecified inferred deontic value.
70	
71	**Other neutrality notes (nonblocking):**
72	- **N3:** TC-4 is incomplete. R-N3's exception codes an *authorize* performative as OPERATOR, not PERFORMATIVE_ONLY. A bare "Slice 7C AUTHORIZED" is then as definitionally paired with its act as "ANNOTATE is adopted", but 4b cannot exclude it. Authorize is the most common operation in this register.
73	- **N4:** D8(ii) is too broad. It turns descriptive or predictive indicatives into norms: R27's "it APPLIES §12"; R-47's "no observable behaviour changes until 7C"; R-77's "Implementation continues under…". This raises counts of norms about work, which leans toward H-B's coupling. The rule is symmetric in form but is a theoretical choice and is not listed.
74	- **N5:** D11's "cites as evidence" and "asserts as its own" can drop every norm a session log or commit reports. That would leave norms only in governance instruments, which leans toward H-D. It is not listed.
75	- **N6:** the boundary between REPORTED and SELF_PERFORMED for register rows that reproduce another actor's ruling or instruction (R02 "RULING AS ISSUED, VERBATIM"; R23 "(Principal Architect instruction)") decides whether these acts survive TC-1 1b.
76	
77	**THEORY-CHOICES assessment.**
78	
79	| TC | Assessment |
80	|---|---|
81	| TC-1 | Correct to list and to treat as inherited. **Incomplete:** it omits self-performed negative dispositions (B1). Its 1a and 1c descriptions are therefore inaccurate. |

83	| TC-3 | Appropriate. r3 codes no force, so this is an analysis choice. Listing it is harmless and useful. |
84	| TC-4 | Appropriate. Incomplete for bare authorize performatives (N3). |
85	| Missing | Self-performed refusals/withdrawals as acts (should be in TC-1). D8(ii) prospective indicatives as norms. D11's treatment of reported or cited norms. ("A standard is never REQUIRED" is a lexical choice, recoverable from `status: <label>`, and acceptably decided.) |
86	| Over-listed | None. No listed choice could have been decided neutrally in the schema. |

88	## 4. Consistency
89	
90	1. **R-A3 bullet ("any other operation → NONE") vs D3 last bullet and A1–A3** (self-performed refusals and withdrawals of any operation are acts). This is B1.
91	2. **D3 is circular and self-contradicting.** R-A3(c) requires SELF_PERFORMED (D3). D3 defines SELF_PERFORMED as "R-A3 (a)–(c) hold", then also assigns it to refusals that fail (a) and (b).

93	4. **D12 vs R-N1 and D8(i).** "Remains candidate" and "stays in…" are both status labels and verdicts. Only the priority order decides, and the result re-levels (N2).
94	5. **R-A1 (retained) vs A3 / R-A2.** R-A1 says "not an ACT_REFUSED unless an *attempt* is recorded". A3 accepts a *proposal*.
95	6. **D4 vs D6.** A PREPARED ruling is a proposal (D4), and "a proposal is not ATTEMPTED" (D6), yet R05 is ATTEMPTED. This is consistent only if the proposal (to adopt) and the attempt (to authorize) are different operations. The schema should say so.
96	7. **The R-A5 merge rule interacts with R-A3's list.** "A deciding act whose content is X is coded as X." The R-36 "Promotion Review ADOPTED", whose content is promotion, can then be coded as *promote*, which gives A7 NONE instead of ACT_OCCURRED adopt. Merging can move an act on or off the closed list.
97	8. **Priority order:**
98	   - ACT: A1–A8 is a complete first-match list for state. Operation selection has no tie-break among candidates at the same step, and "highest step" is unclear.
99	   - NORM: priority applies only *between* classes on the *same* target. Two OPERATOR clauses on one target fall to step 7 UNKNOWN: R12 "MAY BE PLANNED AND MUST NOT BE STARTED"; R34 "AUTHORIZED; engineering may begin RED". So does an unclear target split. Those spans plainly decide, so this contradicts R-A4's meaning of UNKNOWN, and it removes exactly the norm-on-work records from support counts. **The NORM priority order is not complete.**

101	## 5. Codability
102	
103	A fresh coder can apply most of r3 from §1–§5 without reading the rationale: the closed lexicons, the D1 heading test, the first-match tables and R-S1 are all mechanical. The obstacles are:
104	- the circular D3 / R-A3(c);
105	- inferred proposals (§3);
106	- same-class norm ties and same-step act ties;
107	- the D11 / R-N1 contradiction;
108	- multiple operations in D13 (R30; "PLAN AND IMPLEMENT");
109	- D1 depends on how the dataset formats section headings, not on the source text.

115	- **B2.** G3 is not closed on R01. §3 lets a PROPOSAL be an INFERENCE, which reopens coder judgement inside R-A2 and A2/A3. The merge rule also leaves X undecided (resolve vs adopt).
116	  - *Fix:* require the proposal to be stated in words (SOURCE_FACT), and code UNKNOWN otherwise. Fix X as the operation that the refusal verb's complement names.

122	3. Restrict D12's negative-verdict list, or let status labels in a review keep `status: <label>` (N2).
123	4. Tag bare *authorize* performatives so that TC-4 4b can exclude them (N3).
124	5. Narrow D8(ii) to statements that assign a standing, and list the broader reading as a theory choice (N4).
125	6. Fix the D3 circularity. Add a tie-break to R-A5 operation selection and define "highest step".
126	7. Clarify the D4/D6 split (proposal to adopt vs attempt at the instrument's operation). Reconcile R-A1's "attempt" with R-A2/A3's "proposal or attempt".

129	10. Disclose the non-minimal extensions (D7, R-X1, A1/A5, D11, D8(ii)) as scope extensions. Give D13 a rule for spans that name two operations (R30, R05).
